疊音鈸具有明亮而清脆的音色，帶有適度的溫暖感，音域位於中高頻至高頻範圍。其獨特之: The ride cymbal has a bright, clear timbre with a moderate warmth, sitting between the middle-high and high frequencies. What sets it apart is how well it carries: it stands out plainly in an ensemble. Each stroke has layers, giving a clear definite note as well as a warm sustain. Beside a crash cymbal the ride is fuller and rounder, with a longer, deeper resonance; beside a hi-hat it sounds more open and bright. It resonates through the free vibration of the plate, which produces rich overtones and a tone with body. A light tap and a hard strike give different expressions, and it is the voice that keeps the pulse steady in the kit.
疊音鈸屬體鳴，Hornbostel–Sachs 111.24，常見於歐洲鼓組。演: The ride cymbal is an idiophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 111.24, common on European drum kits. It is usually mounted at the far right of the kit, above the floor tom, and struck with the sticks to hold a steady rhythm rather than to accent like a crash. Begin by practising the bow and the bell separately: striking the bow gives a continuous shimmer, striking the bell a brighter, clearer single note. Wooden-tip sticks sound smoother and quieter, nylon-tip sticks more forward; with brushes, or in recording, a thin crash struck gently can also serve as a ride. Besides the open and closed sounds, the ride can take over the rhythm of the hi-hat.
疊音鈸是體鳴樂器，常見於鼓組中，通常置於落地鼓上方、鼓組最右側或慣用手方向。在搖: The ride cymbal is an idiophone found in the drum kit, usually placed above the floor tom, at the far right of the kit or on the player's leading side. In rock, jazz and metal, drummers strike it at regular intervals to hold a steady rhythm and accompany the song; the same figure may be played on the hi-hat in a verse and on the ride in an instrumental or a chorus. With brushes, or in recording, a thin crash can stand in for the ride; in some early rock styles a sizzle cymbal served as a second ride alongside a guitar solo. The flat ride is quieter and is also common on jazz kits.
疊音鈸源於20世紀初的美國爵士樂文化。隨著爵士樂的發展，鼓手們需要一種能夠維持穩: The ride cymbal comes out of American jazz culture in the early twentieth century. As jazz developed, drummers needed a cymbal that could hold a steady pulse, and the ride cymbal answered that need. Against the sharp sound of the crash, the ride offers a rounder, steadier tone, suited to long stretches of continuous playing.
疊音鈸由黃銅合金製成，通常採用B8或B20銅錫合金，提供明亮而溫暖的音色。鈸面經: The ride cymbal is made of a brass alloy, usually B8 or B20 bronze (copper and tin), which gives a bright and warm tone. The surface is hammered and lathed with care, shaping its particular curve of tone. The bell can be made of metal of a different thickness to adjust the sound, and the design of the edge affects the overtone character. Beneath the plate sits a cloth or leather washer on the stand, reducing unwanted vibration.
